issue.title: sase artifact doctor counts refs from an uncloned sidecar as dangling breakage, so link health is workspace-dependent
issue.description: `sase artifact doctor` reports every `research:` ref as a dangling link row in a workspace where the research sidecar is not cloned, mixing "this sidecar is not cloned here" with "this row is broken". The same aggregate reports 2 dangling research refs in a workspace that has the clone and 33 in one that does not.

task_type_fields.impact:
IMPACT: `sase artifact doctor` exits 1 ("unhealthy") and prints a 33-entry breakage list
that is entirely a local-clone artifact, so an agent verifying artifact-link health in
an ephemeral workspace cannot tell real dangling rows from refs whose sidecar simply is
not cloned here. Commit 46fc307d8 ("feat(sase): make beads sidecar lazy-clone by
default", 2026-08-25) makes an uncloned sidecar the normal state rather than the
exception, so this misreport is now the common case rather than a corner.

`--fix` reports rather than deletes these refs, so no data is lost; the cost is a
report that cries wolf and hides the real residue underneath it.

RESIDUE THIS WOULD EXPOSE: after correcting the classification, the genuinely broken
rows this tree still holds are `bead:sase-om` (a row pointing at a bead that no longer
exists), 20 plan-side orphaned `links/` companions whose `.md` is absent from the plans
sidecar, and 3 `file:` companions under ~/tmp/screenshots. Epic sase-tw's
rename-following phase (sase-tw.4) established that none of these are explained by git
rename history and deliberately reports rather than deletes them; they are recorded here
as the expected remainder, not as part of this defect.

FOUND BY the sase-tw land agent (epic "Artifact links that survive, derive themselves,
and pay for the turn") while verifying that epic's link-health counters before closing.
Phase notes sase-tw.4 #1 and #2 proposed repairing the leftovers; this bead is the
distinct, independently reproduced classification defect underneath those reports.
task_type_fields.repro:
REPRODUCTION (2026-08-25, workspace whose `research` sidecar is not cloned; `sase repo
list` shows research CLONED ✗, 4/25 workspaces):

```
$ .venv/bin/python -c "
from pathlib import Path
from sase.sdd.artifact_link_store import resolve_artifact_link_store
s = resolve_artifact_link_store(cwd=Path.cwd())
print({k: (str(v), v.is_dir()) for k, v in s.sidecar_roots.items()})"
{'plan': ('.../sase_12/sase/repos/plans', True),
 'research': ('.../sase_12/sase/repos/research', False)}

$ .venv/bin/python -c "
from sase.artifact_cli.link_health import resolve_cli_reference
print(resolve_cli_reference('research:202608/artifact_link_graph/artifact_link_graph.md').resolution.status)"
missing

$ .venv/bin/sase artifact doctor
... Dangling link refs   bead:sase-om, research:202606/..., research:202608/...   (33 research refs)
```

`_dangling_refs` (src/sase/artifact_cli/link_health.py:305-336) calls
`resolve_cli_reference(ref)` and, when the status is not resolved, appends the ref to
`dangling` for every kind except `agent`. `agent:` already gets its own
"Unpublished agent refs" line, so the classification distinction exists — it is just not
extended to a sidecar root that is absent from this workspace.

The same tree reports a different answer per workspace: phase agent sase-tw.4, running
where the research sidecar was cloned, reported 2 dangling research refs after its
repair pass; this workspace reports 33 for the identical aggregate.

payload.description: the epic whose land-agent verification found this; its phase sase-tw.4 owns the rename-repair pass this report sits on top of, and its phase notes #1/#2 proposed repairing the residue
